notes: Most substantive pre-cutoff filing. Augmented with the Q2 2024 10-Q (0000950170-24-094122) for Aug-2024 forward-looking commentary on the same programs.

claims.claim_text: Rocket Lab is the prime contractor on the Space Development Agency (SDA) Tranche 2 Transport Layer-Beta (T2TL-Beta) program for 18 space vehicles, total contract value $515M ($489M base + $26M incentives/options), awarded Dec 21, 2023 via wholly owned subsidiary Rocket Lab National Security.
claims.subject: Rocket Lab USA, Inc. (via Rocket Lab National Security)
claims.source_quote: On December 21, 2023, we, through our wholly owned subsidiary Rocket Lab National Security, entered into an agreement with the Space Development Agency ("SDA") to design, manufacture, deliver, and operate 18 space vehicles. The contract with the SDA has a total value of $515 million, which includes a base amount of $489 million and incentives and options totaling $26 million.

claims.claim_text: Rocket Lab has a Space Development Agency Tracking Layer T3 prime exposure (per cohort metadata — narrative-load-bearing forward DoD constellation pipeline beyond the T2TL-Beta award).
claims.subject: Rocket Lab USA, Inc.
claims.source_quote: Cohort metadata: 'SDA Tracking Layer T3 prime exposure'. The 10-K describes its constellation-launch + spacecraft-manufacturing strategy as positioned for SDA-style proliferated LEO constellations: 'Neutron will be tailored for commercial and U.S. government constellation launches' and 'Neutron is expected to have the capability of launching nearly all of the spacecraft configurations that we expect to be launched through 2029.'

claims.claim_text: Rocket Lab is developing the Neutron medium-lift launch vehicle under a Space Systems Command (USSF) National Security Space Launch (NSSL) framework, with $20.3M / $3.6M / $0.4M in 2023/22/21 credits recorded for the Neutron upper-stage development agreement.
claims.subject: Rocket Lab USA, Inc.

object_value.agency: U.S. Space Force Space Systems Command

claims.source_quote: The Company entered into an agreement with the U.S. Space Force's Space Systems Command for development of the Neutron launch vehicle's upper stage during the year ended 2021. The Company recorded credits of $20,339, $3,618 and $393 in connection with this award during the year [2023 / 2022 / 2021]. ... 'as a secondary payload on rockets developed under the National Security Space Launch program of the U.S. Space Force.'

claims.claim_text: Rocket Lab is expanding into the hypersonic-test market via HASTE (Hypersonic Accelerator Suborbital Test Electron) — a DoD-customer launch vertical positioned for AFRL / MDA / Army hypersonic test missions.
claims.subject: Rocket Lab USA, Inc.
claims.source_quote: Expand into new launch service verticals, such as Hypersonic Accelerator Suborbital Test Electron ("HASTE").

claims.claim_text: In FY2023, approximately 31% of Rocket Lab's total annual revenues were derived from contracts with the U.S. government, U.S. prime contractors and their agencies (vs 33% in 2022 and 8% in 2021).
claims.subject: Rocket Lab USA, Inc.
claims.source_quote: During 2023, 2022 and 2021, approximately 31%, 33% and 8%, respectively, of our total annual revenues were derived from contracts with the U.S. government, U.S. prime contractors and its agencies or from subcontracts with other U.S. government contractors.

claims.claim_text: Northrop Grumman Space Systems is a top-10% revenue customer at 13% of FY2023 total revenue and 20% of accounts receivable as of Dec 31, 2023 — implying Rocket Lab is a subcontractor on Northrop-prime DoD/NRO programs.
claims.subject: Rocket Lab USA, Inc.
claims.source_quote: Northrop Grumman Space Systems 13% ... MDA Corporation 13% ... [of FY2023 total revenue]; Accounts receivable Dec 31 2023: MDA Corporation 21%, Northrop Grumman Space Systems 20%.

claims.claim_text: Rocket Lab's $1.046B backlog as of Dec 31, 2023 ($248.3M Launch + $797.8M Space Systems) carries forward expected revenue, with ~41% expected within 12 months and 59% beyond 12 months — leaning heavily on DoD-customer constellation work post-SDA award.
claims.subject: Rocket Lab USA, Inc.
claims.source_quote: As of December 31, 2023, our backlog totaled $1,046.1 million, of which $248.3 million is related to Launch and $797.8 million is related to Space Systems. ... Remaining backlog totaled $1,046,126 as of December 31, 2023, of which approximately 41% is expected to be recognized within 12 months, with the remaining 59% to be recognized beyond 12 months.

claims.claim_text: Rocket Lab is a launch services provider to DARPA and NRO for both Electron and (future) Neutron launches, positioning it for DARPA space-experiment PEs and NRO rapid-response launch programs.
claims.subject: Rocket Lab USA, Inc.
claims.source_quote: we have delivered 172 spacecraft to space across 38 successful orbital missions for commercial and government customers, including the United States ... Department of Defense ('DoD'), the National Aeronautics and Space Administration ('NASA'), the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency ('DARPA') and the National Reconnaissance Office ('NRO')

claims.claim_text: Rocket Lab's wholly owned SolAero (acquired Jan 2022) supplies space-grade solar cells/panels used on DoD constellations; SolAero contract-loss provision of $8.0M as of Dec 31 2023 suggests fixed-price SolAero contracts continue to under-deliver.
claims.subject: SolAero Technologies (Rocket Lab subsidiary)
claims.source_quote: In connection with the SolAero acquisition, the Company assumed a contract with a customer to provide solar panel module at a fixed price. The Company determined that it was probable that the costs to complete the solar panel modules as stipulated by the contract would exceed the fixed firm price ... The provision for contract losses outstanding as of December 31, 2023, which primarily is related to the solar panel module agreement, was $8,047.

claims.claim_text: Rocket Lab built/launched ~11 Electron launch vehicles in 2023 with 10 successful missions, and intends to leverage LC-1 (Mahia NZ, two pads) supporting up to 120 missions/yr plus LC-2 (Wallops VA) for DoD rapid-call missions — facility claim that is independently verifiable.
claims.subject: Rocket Lab USA, Inc.
claims.source_quote: LC-1 serves as our high-volume launch complex with two operational launch pads ... capable of supporting up to 120 missions every year. We also operate a dedicated launch pad at NASA's Wallops Flight Facility, at Wallops Island, Virginia, which we refer to as Launch Complex 2 ('LC-2'). LC-2 can support 24-hour rapid call-up capability for defense needs ... is currently licensed to launch 12 missions per year.
